issues.description: The UML in the problem statement declares numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as double, while the solution implementation declares these attributes as int. This creates confusion about the expected data type for student counts and how getTotalNumberOfStudents (declared as returning int in the UML) should behave when summing double values. Students may be uncertain whether to implement the attributes and related methods using int or double.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the student-count types consistent across the problem statement, template, and solution. Either: (a) change the UML and any references in problem_statement.md to declare numberOfInscribedStudents and numberOfGuestStudents as int (and keep getTotalNumberOfStudents returning int), or (b) change the solution and template to use double for those attributes and adjust getTotalNumberOfStudents to return double (and update any tests/examples accordingly). Prefer option (a) if integer counts are intended.
